'''Ehud Hrushovski''' {{post-nominals|country=GBR|FRS}} ({{langx|he|אהוד הרושובסקי}}; born 30 September 1959) is a [[mathematical logician]].<ref name=ETH>{{Cite web|title=Heinz Hopf Prize to a model theorist|url=https://math.ethz.ch/news-and-events/news/d-math-news/2019/10/heinz-hopf-prize-to-a-model-theorist.html|date=23 October 2019|access-date=17 August 2020|website=math.ethz.ch|language=en}}</ref> He is a Merton Professor of Mathematical Logic at the [[University of Oxford]] and a Fellow of [[Merton College, Oxford]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Professor Ehud Hrushovski|url=https://www.merton.ox.ac.uk/people/professor-ehud-hrushovski|access-date=17 August 2020|website=Merton College, Oxford|language=en-GB}}</ref> He was also Professor of Mathematics at the [[Hebrew University of Jerusalem]].<ref name="Academy of Europe: Hrushovski Ehud">{{Cite web|title=Academy of Europe: Hrushovski Ehud|url=https://www.ae-info.org/ae/Member/Hrushovski_Ehud|access-date=17 August 2020|website=www.ae-info.org}}</ref>

==Early life and education==
Hrushovski's father, [[Benjamin Harshav]],<ref>Archives, [[Ghetto Fighters' House]]</ref> was a [[literary theorist]], a Yiddish and Hebrew [[poet]] and a translator, [[professor]] at [[Yale University]] and [[Tel Aviv University]] in [[comparative literature]]. Ehud Hrushovski earned his PhD from the [[University of California, Berkeley]] in 1986 under [[Leo Harrington]]; his dissertation was titled ''Contributions to Stable Model Theory''.<ref>{{mathgenealogy|31791}}</ref> He was a professor of mathematics at the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] until 1994, when he became a professor at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem. Hrushovski moved in 2017 to the University of Oxford, where he is the Merton Professor of Mathematical Logic.<ref name="Academy of Europe: Hrushovski Ehud"/><ref name=ETH/>

==Career==
Hrushovski is well known for several fundamental contributions to [[model theory]], in particular in the branch that has become known as geometric model theory, and its applications.<ref>{{Cite book|last1=Pillay|first1=Anand|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=k6FK_Gqal2EC|title=Geometric Stability Theory|date=1996|publisher=Clarendon Press|isbn=978-0-19-853437-2|language=en}}</ref> His PhD thesis revolutionized [[stable theory|stable model theory]] (a part of model theory arising from the stability theory introduced by [[Saharon Shelah]]). Shortly afterwards he found counterexamples to the [[Trichotomy Conjecture]] of [[Boris Zilber]] and his method of proof has become well known as [[Hrushovski construction]]s and found many other applications since.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Evans|first1=David M.|last2=Ferreira|first2=Marco S.|date=April 2011|title=The geometry of Hrushovski constructions, I. The uncollapsed case|journal=Annals of Pure and Applied Logic|volume=162|issue=6|pages=474–488|doi=10.1016/j.apal.2011.01.008|arxiv=1103.3638|s2cid=3863424}}</ref>

One of his most famous results is his proof of the geometric [[Mordell–Lang conjecture]] in all characteristics using model theory in 1996. This deep proof was a landmark in logic and geometry. He has had many other famous and notable results in model theory and its applications to geometry, algebra, and combinatorics.<ref>{{Cite book|last=Bouscaren|first=Elisabeth|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=lN1tCQAAQBAJ&q=hrushovski+mordell+lang|title=Model Theory and Algebraic Geometry: An introduction to E. Hrushovski's proof of the geometric Mordell-Lang conjecture|date=14 March 2009|publisher=Springer|isbn=978-3-540-68521-0|language=en}}</ref>

=== Honours and awards ===
He was an invited speaker at the 1990 [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] and a plenary speaker at the 1998 [[International Congress of Mathematicians|ICM]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.mathunion.org/icm-plenary-and-invited-speakers|title=ICM Plenary and Invited Speakers|author=<!--Not stated-->|publisher=[[International Mathematical Union]]|access-date=22 July 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite book|author=Hrushovski, Ehud|chapter=Geometrical model theory|title=Doc. Math. (Bielefeld) Extra Vol. ICM Berlin, 1998, vol. I|year=1998|pages=281–302|chapter-url=https://www.elibm.org/ft/10011725000}}</ref> He is a recipient of the [[Erdős Prize]] of the [[Israel Mathematical Union]] in 1994, the Rothschild Prize in 1998, the [[Karp Prize]] of the [[Association for Symbolic Logic]] in 1993 (jointly with [[Alex Wilkie]]) and again in 1998,<ref>{{cite web |url=https://aslonline.org/asl-information/prizes-and-awards/karp-prize-recipients/ |title=Karp Prize Recipients |publisher=[[Association for Symbolic Logic]] |access-date=22 July 2019 |archive-date=22 July 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190722150030/https://aslonline.org/asl-information/prizes-and-awards/karp-prize-recipients/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> In 2007, he was honored with holding the [[Gödel Lecture]]. In his absence, a lecture on his work titled ''Algebraic Model Theory'' was given by Thomas Scanlon.<ref>{{Cite journal|date=2007|title=2007 Annual Meeting of the Association for Symbolic Logic|url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/4493334|journal=The Bulletin of Symbolic Logic|volume=13|issue=3|pages=386–408|doi=10.2178/bsl/1186666153|jstor=4493334|s2cid=124193052|issn=1079-8986|last1=Džamonja|first1=Mirna|url-access=subscription}}</ref> In 2019 he was awarded the [[Heinz Hopf Prize]]<ref name=ETH/> and in 2022 the [[Shaw Prize]] in Mathematical Sciences.<ref>[https://www.shawprize.org/prizes/mathematical-sciences Shaw Prize 2022]</ref>

Hrushovski is a fellow of the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]] (2007),<ref>{{Cite web|title=Ehud Hrushovski|url=https://www.amacad.org/person/ehud-hrushovski|access-date=17 August 2020|website=American Academy of Arts & Sciences|language=en}}</ref> and [[Israel Academy of Sciences and Humanities]] (2008). He was elected a [[Fellow of the Royal Society]] in 2020.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://royalsociety.org/people/Ehud-Hrushovski-25359/|title=Ehud Hrushovski|publisher=Royal Society|access-date= 19 September 2020}}</ref>
